name: Attention Restoration Theory
citation: Kaplan, S. (1995). The restorative benefits of nature: Toward an integrative framework. Journal of Environmental Psychology, 15(3), 169-182.

constructs.description: Gentle, effortless engagement with moderately interesting stimuli permitting reflective thought. Neural signature: medial temporal DMN subsystem engagement + dorsal medial subsystem suppression.
Cognitive disengagement from habitual concerns through hippocampal context reconstruction. Requires perceptual discontinuity sufficient to trigger new context model.
Environmental richness and structure sufficient for immersion. Scope (hierarchical prediction depth) + Coherence (prediction transferability via fractal self-similarity).
Match between person's current goals and environmental supports/demands. Incompatibility generates dACC error monitoring, consuming the attentional resource restoration replenishes.

schema_gaps: Bottom-up mutual manipulability for DMN ↔ soft fascination not yet directly tested
Olfactory channel effects on fascination (~25 staging rows unaccounted)
irreducible_residual.narrative: The four-construct syndrome (Soft Fascination, Being Away, Extent, Compatibility) — the claim that these four specific constructs form a coherent restoration pattern — is not derivable from any single T1 framework. Compatibility is inherently person-dependent: the same environment may be highly compatible for one person and deeply incompatible for another. This person-dependence cannot be reduced to environmental features alone.

key_references: Berman, M.G., Jonides, J., & Kaplan, S. (2008). Psychol. Sci., 19(12), 1207-1212.
Andrews-Hanna, J.R., Smallwood, J., & Spreng, R.N. (2014). Ann. N.Y. Acad. Sci., 1316(1), 29-52.

function_form.function_form: R(t) = R_max - D(t) + α·∫₀ᵗ [SF(s) · BA(s) · E(s)]ds

variables.R(t): Attentional resource level at time t
variables.\u03b1: Restoration rate constant (~0.3/hr for natural environments)

predictions: Natural environments restore directed attention faster than urban (α_nature ≈ 2.5 × α_urban)
Restoration follows sigmoid: fast recovery early, diminishing returns after ~20 min

provenance.seminal_paper: Kaplan, S. (1995). The restorative benefits of nature: Toward an integrative framework. JEP, 15(3), 169-182.
provenance.predecessor: William James' voluntary vs involuntary attention (1892); Olmsted's restorative landscapes (1865)
provenance.historical_context: Developed to explain why natural environments restore mental fatigue. Extended James' attention typology with environmental factors. Became dominant framework in environmental psychology alongside SRT.
